openClinicalQuestions: Dr. Zalak: which entry-level cues (if any) she wants named on-site versus reserved for supervised sessions, given the guardrail against publishing specific exercises without contraindication review.

claimLedger.claim: Core = tummy, diaphragm, pelvic floor; avoid early sit-ups/crunches/plank; build walking and gentle core work; graded physio programme.
claimLedger.sourceSection: POGP · Tummy muscle separation (DRAM) in pregnancy · not stated
claimLedger.limitations: UK leaflet; not a full exercise prescription

claimLedger.claim: Avoid sit-ups, planks and high-impact early; pelvic-floor and deep stomach exercises may help; seek GP if gap still obvious around 8 weeks.
claimLedger.sourceSection: NHS · Your post-pregnancy body · not stated on fetched page
claimLedger.limitations: UK public advice; individual wounds/symptoms alter timing

claimLedger.claim: Start a little early and build slowly; strengthen abdominal and pelvic-floor muscles to help reduce leakage, heaviness and back/pelvic pain.
claimLedger.sourceSection: POGP · Exercise and Advice After Pregnancy · Publication date on catalogue page 29 Nov 2022
claimLedger.limitations: Booklet exercises still need personal screening for wounds and pelvic-floor dysfunction
